input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: The indemnity package meets our preferred position. Section 20.1 gives a full Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims covering Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel, with no customer-modification or combination carve-outs. Section 20.2 adds Vendor indemnities for breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud. Section 20.4 sets standard reciprocal procedure (prompt notice with a material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at the indemnifier's expense, control of defence, settlement consent protections), and 20.5 provides the procure/modify-or-replace/terminate-and-refund remedies (cross-referenced by the termination right in 9.3). Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 stays narrow — unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised and Customer's own violation of law — with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and instructions. Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3, so they sit outside the general liability cap, which is better than the fallback's 3× super-cap. No redline needed.
